name: Getting Things Done (GTD) Ubiquitous Capture
diagnostic: Open-loop cognitive overload and intrusive retrieval spikes. Unprocessed mental inputs disrupt sustained focus by cyclically demanding conscious awareness via the Zeigarnik effect.

procedure.text: Keep one inbox reachable from every environment in under three seconds.
Record every commitment, request, idea or question as an atomic entry the moment it appears.
Do not categorize, edit or prioritize while capturing; keep recording separate from evaluating.
Flush the inbox to zero at least once a day in a dedicated triage window.

trap: Capturing into deep folders or taxonomies. Categorizing at the capture point forces an evaluation, so logging is postponed and the brain keeps the task instead.
procedureFull:
1. Establish a single, universally accessible inbox medium available across all operative environments in under three seconds.
2. The instant a commitment, request, idea, or unresolved question crosses conscious awareness, record it as an atomic text entry without categorization, editing, or prioritization.
3. Prohibit real-time processing during capture; maintain complete separation between recording and evaluating.
4. Flush this inbox buffer to zero at least once daily during dedicated triage windows.
setupFull:
inbox.md
  * [ ] Investigate connection pool timeout in staging database
  * [ ] Schedule Q3 performance review sync with engineering lead
  * [ ] Research WebAssembly compilation pipeline for text parser
trapFull: Capturing directly into deep folder hierarchies or taxonomies. Categorization friction at the capture point forces prefrontal evaluation, causing practitioners to postpone logging and revert to biological retention.
